title: Generic-stalk compatibility of the differential of a dominant morphism
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X,Y$ be integral $k$-schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-scheme-over-base], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose image is dense. Write $\eta_X,\eta_Y$ for the generic points [def-sc-generic-point] and $L=\mathcal O_{X,\eta_X}=k(X)$, $K=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}=k(Y)$ [def-sc-function-field]. Use module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], differential sheaves [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], and Kähler differential modules [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Suppose $\alpha_Z:(\Omega_{Z/k})_{\eta_Z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{k(Z)/k}$ is a $k(Z)$-linear isomorphism for each $Z=X,Y$, satisfying $\alpha_Z((da)_{\eta_Z})=d(a_{\eta_Z})$ for every regular function $a$ on any nonempty open of $Z$. Then $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$. Let $\varphi:K\to L$ be the resulting map of structure-sheaf stalks (the induced function-field map). With module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], there is an $L$-linear isomorphism
$$\beta_f:(f^*\Omega_{Y/k})_{\eta_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}L\otimes_K\Omega_{K/k},$$
where the tensor product uses $\varphi$, such that $\beta_f((f^*s)_{\eta_X})=1\otimes\alpha_Y(s_{\eta_Y})$ for every local section $s$ of $\Omega_{Y/k}$ near $\eta_Y$; $f^*s$ denotes the pullback-adjunction unit. For the canonical differential $df$ [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map], the map $\alpha_X\circ(df)_{\eta_X}\circ\beta_f^{-1}$ is the $L$-linear map
$$L\otimes_K\Omega_{K/k}\longrightarrow\Omega_{L/k},\qquad a\otimes db\longmapsto a\,d\varphi(b).$$

source.place: Tag 01UV (lemma-functoriality-differentials), characterization on local sections, evaluated on germs at generic points; scalar-extension coordinates supplied by sheaves.tex, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules.

proof.text: First identify the points and the field map. By [def-pc-integral-scheme] the spaces are nonempty and irreducible, and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] supplies their unique generic points. For any closed subset $C\subseteq Y$ containing $f(\eta_X)$, continuity of $f$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism] makes $f^{-1}C$ closed and containing $\eta_X$, hence all of $X$ by [def-sc-generic-point]. Thus $C$ contains $f(X)$ and, by density, all of $Y$. Consequently $f(\eta_X)$ is generic and equals $\eta_Y$. The induced stalk homomorphism $\varphi:K\to L$ sends a germ $a_{\eta_Y}$ to $(f^\sharp a)_{\eta_X}$ by the definition of a locally ringed space morphism. It respects $k$ because the structure morphisms commute with $f$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

source.place: Tags 01RM (lemma-dominant-finite-number-irreducible-components), 0CC1 (lemma-dominant-between-integral), generic-point argument in their proofs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-pullback] with $x=\eta_X$ and $\mathcal G=\Omega_{Y/k}$ to obtain $\rho:(f^*\Omega_{Y/k})_{\eta_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Omega_{Y/k})_{\eta_Y}\otimes_K L$, formed using precisely $\varphi$, and $\rho((f^*s)_{\eta_X})=s_{\eta_Y}\otimes1$. Define $\beta_f$ by following $\rho$ with $m\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes\alpha_Y(m)$. The latter map is well defined by tensor bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $K$-linearity of $\alpha_Y$; its inverse is $a\otimes\omega\mapsto\alpha_Y^{-1}(\omega)\otimes a$. Both maps are $L$-linear and their composites fix every pure tensor, so they are inverse on the tensor products, which are generated by pure tensors. This gives the required $L$-linear isomorphism and its section formula $\beta_f((f^*s)_{\eta_X})=1\otimes\alpha_Y(s_{\eta_Y})$.

source.place: Tag 0098, lemma-stalk-pullback-modules; compose its isomorphism with the given alpha_Y and the explicit tensor flip.

proof.text: The assignment $b\mapsto d\varphi(b)$ is a $k$-derivation $K\to\Omega_{L/k}$, where $K$ acts through $\varphi$: additivity, the Leibniz rule and vanishing on $k$ follow directly from those of $d$ and the $k$-algebra homomorphism $\varphi$. By [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] it induces a $K$-linear map $u:\Omega_{K/k}\to\Omega_{L/k}$ with $u(db)=d\varphi(b)$. Tensor bilinearity [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] gives the $L$-linear map $T:L\otimes_K\Omega_{K/k}\to\Omega_{L/k}$, $T(a\otimes\omega)=a\,u(\omega)$: the balancing relation holds since $u(c\omega)=\varphi(c)u(\omega)$. In particular $T(a\otimes db)=a\,d\varphi(b)$. The quotient presentation in the differential definition says that the $db$ generate $\Omega_{K/k}$ over $K$; pure tensors generate the tensor product. Therefore the $1\otimes db$ generate $L\otimes_K\Omega_{K/k}$ over $L$.

source.place: Tags 00RO (lemma-universal-omega), 00CX (lemma-tensor-product); their universal properties and generator presentations.

proof.text:
It remains to compare the two $L$-linear maps on these generators. Every $b\in K=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$ is a germ $a_{\eta_Y}$ for a regular function $a$ on a neighbourhood $V$ of $\eta_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Its inverse image is a nonempty neighbourhood of $\eta_X$ by Step 1. The hypothesis on $\alpha_Y$ and Step 2 give $\beta_f((f^*(da))_{\eta_X})=1\otimes db$. The section characterization of $df$ [def-a1-relative-differentials-pullback-map] says $df(f^*(da))=d(f^\sharp a)$. Passing to germs commutes with a module morphism by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], so the hypothesis on $\alpha_X$ gives
$$\alpha_X((df)_{\eta_X}((f^*(da))_{\eta_X}))=\alpha_X((d(f^\sharp a))_{\eta_X})=d((f^\sharp a)_{\eta_X})=d\varphi(b).$$
Thus $\alpha_X\circ(df)_{\eta_X}\circ\beta_f^{-1}$ and $T$ agree on every $1\otimes db$. By the spanning conclusion of Step 3 and $L$-linearity they agree on the whole module, proving the final formula for every $a\otimes db$.

source.place: Tag 01UV (lemma-functoriality-differentials), final characterization on local sections, passed to germs using sheaves.tex Tags 0078 and 007J.
